title: Oscar and the Compass
premise: In the winter of 1918, Zephyrine Pemberton keeps the Gullwrack Point lighthouse alone, having buried her husband, her name, and her past in that order. When a half-drowned stranger washes ashore carrying letters in the handwriting of her brother Oscar — declared dead at Gallipoli four years earlier — she realizes he faked his death to escape a war-crimes cover-up, and the letters are his insurance. As armistice negotiations stall and military historians race to fix the official record, Zephyrine must decide whether twenty years of careful silence are worth more than her brother's truth. The novel ends with Zephyrine testifying before a civilian inquiry, surrendering her anonymity to save Oscar's testimony from being buried — and choosing the found family of witnesses over the safety of invisibility.
about_author: Vesper Sandoval is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the North Atlantic coast. They write historical fiction about people history tried to leave out of its ledgers.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Fog
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A routine storm season opens: lamp trimmed, log kept, silences maintained. We learn how she counts her days in tasks and what she refuses to remember. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returns
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. After a violent gale she finds a man half-dead on the shingle, clutching an oilskin packet. Among his effects: letters in Oscar's unmistakable hand — her brother, dead four years. Emotional beat: shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: A Stranger Named Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, feverish and fragmented. He wakes in the keeper's cottage, assessing whether this woman is rescuer or threat. He was hired to deliver the packet; he doesn't know to whom or why. Emotional beat: wary mutual dependence.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Silences
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, flashback braided with present. How she became invisible: a marriage of convenience, a name traded away, letters never sent. She burns one of Oscar's letters rather than read it. Emotional beat: fear disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Recovering, he reads what he carried: detailed accounts of a village shelling ordered by British officers, documented by a soldier officially among the dead. Emotional beat: dawning horror at what he's been holding.

chapters.title: Visitors from the Ministry
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Two men arrive claiming to search for a missing courier. Their questions are too precise; their courtesy too rehearsed. She lies fluently for the first time in years. Emotional beat: the old skills waking up.

chapters.title: Oscar, Alive, Somewhere
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He reveals the letters were meant to reach a journalist in Cork by month's end — a deadline now impossible. Zephyrine admits Oscar is her brother. Emotional beat: alliance formed out of necessity, not trust.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse as Evidence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She deciphers Oscar's cipher hidden in tide tables appended to the letters — locations, dates, names of officers. The lighthouse that hid her becomes the vault that could expose them. Emotional beat: purpose displacing dread.

chapters.title: Mrs. Calloway's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Wren's POV. The village postmistress, a deserter fisherman, and a widowed nurse form an improvised network. Found family theme crystallizes around Zephyrine's stove. Emotional beat: warmth as risk.

chapters.title: The Historian's Advance Party
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A polite academic arrives compiling 'the official narrative' for the peace delegation, interviewing keepers along the coast. He is not cruel — which makes him more dangerous. Emotional beat: corruption wearing a decent face.

chapters.title: What Wren Carried Away
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, confession chapter. He once informed on a striking dockworker to feed his family; the packet is his penance. Zephyrine must weigh his guilt against his usefulness. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The Ministry men return with a warrant and find the cottage searched, the oilskin gone — because Mrs. Calloway moved it. But they take Wren for questioning. Emotional beat: protection failing those she promised to keep safe.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Watch
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, night vigil. Alone with the decoded evidence, she drafts two versions of the coming days: one where she stays silent, one where she speaks. The lamp turns above her like a conscience. Emotional beat: the cost of each choice made visible.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Barracks Gate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Held for 'routine inquiries,' he stalls his interrogators using details of tides and shipping. The fisherman deserter engineers a clumsy, terrifying extraction. Emotional beat: ordinary people doing extraordinary, unlawful good.

chapters.title: Armistice Rumors
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. News spreads that signing may come within days — after which all wartime records seal for decades. The deadline hardens: get the truth on record now or lose it to the victors' historians. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening resolve into plan.

chapters.title: The Compass Pointing Home
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A final letter surfaces in Oscar's cipher revealing where he waits: a Quaker safe house outside Dublin, too ill to travel, trusting her with everything. Title meaning lands — his compass points not north but to her. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into mission.

chapters.title: Crossing to Cork
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Wren's alternating POV. A perilous run down the coast by fishing boat, pursued by a patrol launch, the evidence sewn into Zephyrine's coat. Emotional beat: terror shared is terror halved.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Room
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Before a civilian commission convened hastily ahead of the armistice, she gives her name — her real one — for the first time in twenty years, and enters Oscar's testimony into the record. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed through witness.

chapters.title: The Victor's Pen
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The historian attempts to discredit her; the nurse and postmistress testify in turn, corroborating dates and shipments. The room shifts. The officer named in the letters is summoned. Emotional beat: power contested publicly, at last.

chapters.title: Signature and Seal
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Armistice day. The inquiry adjourns without verdict but with the testimony entered and copied — three copies, three hands, unsealable. The Ministry men withdraw. Emotional beat: imperfect victory, honestly won.

chapters.title: Oscar
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She travels to the safe house and finds her brother diminished, alive, unrepentant about the lie that kept him dead. Their reckoning is quiet and unfinished. Emotional beat: love that survives being tested by truth.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Light, Keeper of the Record
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, coda. Spring returns to Gullwrack Point. Wren stays on as assistant keeper; the found family gathers at her table. She writes the true account of the great storms in the official log — signed. Emotional beat: silence finally chosen freely, not imposed.
